instructor:
His lectures were more than enjoyable. It is obvious that his knowledge in cognitive psychology and neuroscience is profound, and that he is skilled in lecturing. This distinguishes him from other professors, given that most professors at Bilkent are, and I'm sorry to say this, incapable of delivering exciting lectures. 

YET, in some instances, he was incredibly impolite and even intimidating. This is presumably the worst aspect of him. For example, when he was asked whether the deadline he set for the homework assignment is mistaken, he not only felt offended by this, he briefly threatened students who sent an e-mail asking for clarification with not extending the deadline exclusively for them -other students could enjoy one more day. Thank god, he didn't do this. The reason we asked whether the deadline set was mistaken was that he previously declared the deadline date as 23rd of December, and that deadline was on 23rd of December but at 00:00, which practically makes Tuesday night the deadline. Since some students know that some professors, in different courses, have made the mistake of choosing 00:00 instead of 23:59 -this changes the due date by 24 hours-, those students asked for clarification. There is nothing condescending in this, I believe, given that EVERYONE CAN MAKE MISTAKES.

The reason why I'm making such a fuss about this is not only because I found his threatening of my friends -and me- absurd and inappropriate, I also have a personal reason. The day he threatened us was already a terrible day for me because I was going through some sort of a depression at the time, wasn't able to sleep, and bogged down with too many deadlines. Seeing a professor whom I admired until then carelessly threatening me by tightening my work schedule killed my morale.  Looking at his previous evaluations, I see that he learns from students' criticisms. I hope he will continue this trend not only to improve his style of lecturing but his communication with students.
